title: Alan Wake Dev’s Forgotten TV-Action Game Hybrid Is At A Huge Discount Right Now
summary: I loved Quantum Break . In fact, I dare say that I still love it to this day. Combining Remedy’s pizzazz for third-person shooters with the boldness to add TV show elements to the narrative experience, Quantum Break’s time-bending power fantasy is one that hooked me from start to finish. After playing it at launch, I let the dust settle before playing it once again in the early 2020s, and now, it’s time for another playthrough—and you may as well join me when it’s this cheap. After Alan Wake’s horror-led approach, with Stephen King vibes oozing from the entire experience, I don’t think any of us expected it to become a larger part of a connected universe. Quantum Break may not officially be part of the same universe, but it feels like the foundation of what would eventually become Remedy’s connected universe. You play as Jack Joyce, who, after catching up with his time-machine-making friend Paul Serene, is interrupted by Jack’s brother, Will, who says using it will cause time to end. Of course, if that happened, the game wouldn’t continue. Instead, both Jack and Paul are afflicted by chronon radiation, giving the pair time-related abilities. Soldiers appear, causing a ruckus on the university campus, led by an older, more dangerous Paul. Gasp! It’s no surprise that a narrative focusing on time-travel shenanigans offers, well, time-travel shenanigans. But between missions, you’ll get to see real actors playing the characters in a series-style format, which gives you a nice break between some incredibly fun missions. That’s right, Remedy’s continued prowess in third-person shooter action is still here, and the time abilities give you some truly fun ways to deal with enemies. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w-aAWXKZS9M You can send out bubbles that freeze enemies in place, fire a barrage of bullets into them, and watch them die a horrible death by countless simultaneous bullets. A dash lets you close the gap between Jack and any enemies giving you trouble from a distance, while a blast lets you levitate Monarch’s helpless soldiers into the air, making them vulnerable to your attacks. You can see Remedy’s vision for future games coming into play here—between Alan Wake 2’s heavy embrace of live-action moments and Control’s suite of powers, those games owe a lot to Quantum Break. If you’re looking to give it a try, and I suggest you do, you can grab Quantum Break for just $8.40 / £6.30 at Fanatical . As a Remedy fan, it’s a truly exciting game to play through because you can see the developer’s vision years before Control and Alan Wake 2’s success. But as a general player, it’s a solid third-person shooter that blends a variety of genres to create something cinematic. Disclosure: GameSpot and Fanatical are both owned by Fandom. title: All GTA 6 Book Swap Locations
summary: Those who grew up in the 80s and 90s would remember things known as gamebooks, the precursors to modern-day role-playing and narrative-driven games. You might recall the Choose Your Own Adventure series and R.L. Stine’s Give Yourself Goosebumps, which presented you with choices, making you turn page after page to see the outcome. Further back, we had classics like the Sorcery series and The Warlock of Firetop Mountain--co-written by authors Steve Jackson and Ian Livingstone, who coincidentally also founded Games Workshop (yes, the very company that owns Warhammer). Grand Theft Auto 6 pays homage to these works in the form of book swap locations, which you can find all over Leonida. In This Article Book Swap collectibles in Grand Theft Auto 6 Book Swaps in Mariana County Book Swap #1 Book Swap #2 Book Swap #3 Book Swaps in Vice-Dale County Book Swap #4 Book Swap #5 Book Swaps in Leonard County and Kelly County Book Swap #6 Book Swap #7 Book Swap collectibles in Grand Theft Auto 6 The book swaps in GTA 6 can be found in public bookcases outside homes--i.e. akin to little free libraries. Once you spot one, interact with it to browse the book’s contents. Yes, they function similarly to magazines and comics in that you can read a few excerpts. However, they’re part of a separate tally in the Collections page. The literary works have silly dilemmas and humorous outcomes. It’s not quite interactive as, say, Tenebrae Lux on the JoyStation, but it’s still a nice nod that fans of gamebooks would appreciate. Book Swaps in Mariana County Book Swap #1 Pick Your Path: Horror - Killer Prom Location: Inside a turtle-shaped container in the northeastern end of Dolphin Drive. Book Swap #2 Pick Your Path: Fantasy - The Wizard’s Ruin Location: Found in Beaumont Avenue in Watson Bay. It’s inside a blue bookcase in front of a white house. Book Swap #3 Pick Your Path: Western - Badland’s Revenge Location: This Book Swap in GTA 6 is in the wealthy neighborhood of Capri in the northwestern part of Mariana County. Go to Viola Street and look for the Halloween House, which also happens to be a WAiNK Curiosity . Book Swaps in Vice-Dale County Book Swap #4 Pick Your Path: Romance - Thighlander Location: Found on SW 3rd Avenue in Southside. Book Swap #5 Pick Your Path: Mystery - Goodnight, Dollface, Goodnight Location: Go to Neptune Circle on Vespucci Island, which is in the northern part of the lake in Vice City. Book Swaps in Leonard County and Kelly County Book Swap #6 Pick Your Path: Survival - Outback Gas Junkie Location: Head to Mamey Circle in the subdivision south of Waning Sands. Look for a large mushroom bookcase in the driveway. Oh, and be sure to open the garage door so you can grab a Liberty City Swingers collectible card. Book Swap #7 Pick Your Path: Sci-Fi - Humanity Versus Space Location: Drive to Reservoir Street, which is across the river northeast of Ambrosia. title: All NoFlusher Tags In GTA 6
summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has several moments that rely heavily on over-the-top silliness. One, in particular, involves poo. Specifically, it’s about a group of individuals who do not want people to waste their, uh, waste, for fear of cloning and other sinister machinations. So, when you’re ready, it’s time to meet the gang and collect the NoFlusher Tags. In This Article The NoFlusher narrative arcs in Grand Theft Auto 6 NoFlusher tag locations NoFlusher Tag #1 NoFlusher Tag #2 NoFlusher Tag #3 NoFlusher Tag #4 NoFlusher Tag #5 NoFlusher Tag #6 NoFlusher Tag #7 NoFlusher Tag #8 NoFlusher Tag #9 NoFlusher Tag #10 NoFlusher Tag #11 NoFlusher Tag #12 NoFlusher Tag #13 NoFlusher Tag #14 NoFlusher Tag #15 Where to find CantCloneThis89’s hideout Andrew Node’s home and NoFlusher Tags reward: The Truffade Thrax How To Complete The Final Flush Meet Dr. Merle and follow his directions The sewage treatment plant What should you do with Dr. Merle? The NoFlusher narrative arcs in Grand Theft Auto 6 If you’ve been gathering collectibles all over Leonida, you’ve likely chanced upon a strange WAiNK Curiosity , that of a NoFlushers Homestead. One pamphlet that’s been left behind even coerces citizens to avoid flushing their feces down the toilet. Instead, folks are encouraged to turn poop into odd by-products like pottery, soap, and even organic food. It’s downright disgusting, but it’s guaranteed to make you chuckle, too. Now, assuming you’ve made your way to Vice City, you’ll be given the opportunity to join the group proper: First, you need to use the WAiNK app on your phone to scan the “Stop! Don’t Flush! #NoFlushers” QR code. You can find this poster/QR code in public bathrooms, like the one in Dynamix Gym just north of your safehouse in chapter 3. Once you’ve done that, someone will tell you to meet up at Frank’s Waffles, and you’ll be able to mark the location on your map. This leads to a mission called The Final Flush. At the same time, you can stumble upon a mystery where you look for NoFlusher Tags in GTA 6. Your goal here is to look for utility markings/scribbles on pavements and roads. NoFlusher tag locations The GTA 6 NoFlusher Tags appear as light blue scribbles with a toilet symbol drawn for good measure. The moment you scan your first one, you’ll get invited to a group chat by none other than Cal. Several members with aliases then welcome you to the group, and you learn that they’re on the lookout for someone named Andrew Node. It seems that Node has been extracting everyone’s excrement to create a clone army using DNA. You’re then tasked by the other members to scan utility markings with your WAiNK app. There are a total of 15 NoFlusher Tags in Vice City, though you only need to scan 10 to progress to the next stage of the mission. NoFlusher Tag #1 Along the sidewalk on Koko Boulevard just past the bridge that leads to Ocean Beach. NoFlusher Tag #2 Near the southern tip of Shore Drive right across from the Janus building. NoFlusher Tag #3 Directly north of the second tag. It’s on the sidewalk across The Buckingham. NoFlusher Tag #4 Continue north along Shore Drive until you’re slightly past Muscle Sands. Then, look to your left and check the area in front of the Daiquiri Bar. NoFlusher Tag #5 From Shore Drive, go west to the Rococo Rich jewelry store, which should have its own icon on the map. NoFlusher Tag #6 At the junction of Huevo Street, off to the side of the Bean Machine coffee shop. NoFlusher Tag #7 Head to Portside Lane in the western portion of Ocean Beach. You’ll see this GTA 6 NoFlusher Tag along the bend on the road. NoFlusher Tag #8 Keep going north from where you got NoFlushers Tag #7. Eventually, you’ll reach Harborside Avenue. The scribbles are on the sidewalk just before the tiny roundabout. NoFlusher Tag #9 This is on Cabega Street just southeast of the above scannable object. It’s outside a Tootsie Katz - All You Can Eat Shrimp restaurant. NoFlusher Tag #10 Found along D Street. It’s outside a Fuji Kitchen with a “free ramen on your birthday” promotion. The Shorefront - Ocean Beach bank is also nearby. NoFlusher Tag #11 Found on Barlow Street. The drawing is in front of the cafe and restroom sheds. NoFlusher Tag #12 Scan this marking along Oleander Boulevard on Oldby Island. It’s by the side of the road that leads to the bridge. NoFlusher Tag #13 Found on the sidewalk outside the Hide Tide Hotel and Restaurant. NoFlusher Tag #14 In front of a large residential complex’s fountain on Northside Avenue. NoFlusher Tag #15 Keep heading north-northeast and scan this drawing along Mariposa Avenue. Where to find CantCloneThis89’s hideout After you scan at least 10 NoFlusher Tags, people in the group will start to panic, saying that Node knows their intentions. As your buddies leave the chat, you receive a DM from the moderator--CantCloneThis89--saying that you should meet him in his hideout. It’s marked on your map, so just head there when you’re able to. Upon arriving at the storage unit, read the note and flip it. At the back, you’ll see the code 8-5-5-4-0-1-3 . Interact with the keypad and input the code to open the unit. Inside, you’ll see how far gone CantCloneThis89 seems to be. In any case, check the boards to glean more clues: The map has an island in the middle encircled. Open the laptop and read the info about Andrew Node’s address. He lives in Sabal Circle, Starfish Island. (It’s the second house on the right.) Some messages in the laptop imply that CantCloneThis89 doesn’t know if he’s still a real person or if he’s been cloned. Andrew Node’s home and NoFlusher Tags reward: The Truffade Thrax You might think that it’s a good idea to drive to Starfish Island. Well, no, that simply won’t do. It’s a gated community, and the guards will warn you to leave. If you keep pestering them, they might fight back or call the cops. Here are our suggestions: Open the map and click on the house’s location on Starfish Island. Then, call a RydeMe so you can fast travel there. When you get out, one security guard will accost you. Eliminate him silently to avoid alerting others. Next, bring down the two guards inside the yard. Once the coast is clear, open the garage door to receive an awesome prize. It’s none other than a Truffade Thrax. This vehicle, which looks like a Bugatti Chiron, happens to be one of the fastest cars in the entire game. Registering this vehicle is very costly, as it requires $70,000 cash. If you don’t have a lot to spare, you can leave it in a garage or in the two parking spaces in your safehouse. That way, it won’t disappear forever. How To Complete The Final Flush The Final Flush mission takes you on a quick romp to learn about Andrew Node’s plots… and where all the poop seems to be going. Remember that fella who contacted you after you scanned the QR code? Well, you might want to visit Frank’s Waffles, so go ahead and track the mission on your map. Meet Dr. Merle and follow his directions The Final Flush in GTA 6 introduces you to Dr. Merle, another conspiracy theorist and NoFlushers member who seeks to learn more about Andrew Node’s fiendishly fecal plans. When you chat with him in the restaurant, he’ll tell you that he swallowed a tracker, which he’ll flush down the toilet. This leads to a sequence where you need to drive Dr. Merle around Vice City. The waypoint disappears intermittently, but Dr. Merle gives you instructions--i.e. Go south, go east, go straight, and the like. Whatever he says, make sure you look at the orientation of your minimap so that you’re going in the right direction. The sewage treatment plant Eventually, the waypoint will appear, and it will guide you to the sewage treatment plant. Merle remarks that this is how Node collects DNA specimens. All the waste materials that get flushed end up in the plant. Merle will attempt to lockpick the gate and a security guard in a vehicle will approach. You can try to defuse the situation, though it’s possible to miss the prompt if Merle is still speaking. (We were unable to respond during our playthrough, but that was fine since the guard still went on his merry way.) In the generator room, wait for Merle to say that the tracker is directly below you. Then, go upstairs and interact with the control panel. Click the second and third buttons on the left, then press the button in the middle. This will reveal a hidden passageway to the cloning vat. What should you do with Dr. Merle? Dr. Merle is aghast upon seeing what he believes to be a cloning vat, and he feels that it’s his responsibility to see where it leads. He goes inside the vat, which slowly fills with icky water. He’ll tell you that you need to press the button to flush him (wherever that may lead). Here’s what happens depending on your decision regarding Dr. Merle in GTA 6: If you decide to ignore Merle’s order, he’ll drown due to the water in the vat. If you decide to flush Merle, he’ll disappear and the vat will be empty. Around this time, the guards will have caught wind of you, and they’ll call the police soon enough: If you wait in the room, you still have to fight the guards and the cops, before you make your escape. If you go inside the cloning vat, it will fill with water and you’ll get flushed down, just like Dr. Merle. Assuming you chose the latter, you’ll receive a permanent stamina boost for your characters. This concludes these two quests about the NoFlushers in GTA 6. However, something more unnerving awaits later. If you sail to Frampton Island north of Lummox County, you’ll discover a hidden bunker. Input this code-- 3-6-1-2 --and check what’s inside. title: Where To Find All 1010 Murals In GTA 6 To Get A Free Car And Garage
summary: Around halfway through Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s campaign, you’ll reach Vice City. You’ll spend several hours just tackling missions and gathering collectibles. While you’re at it, we encourage you to look for the 1010 Murals as well. That’s because this activity is somewhat missable and the rewards--the ‘95 Grotti Cheetah and a free garage--are things you definitely want. In This Article 1010 Murals activity requirement and mechanics Map: 1010 Murals in Vice City Mural #1: Compliance Theater Mural #2: Extraction Service Mural #3: Loophole Architecture Mural #4: You Signed the Terms and Conditions Mural #5: Privatized Pains Socialized Gains 1010 Murals reward location 1010 Murals activity requirement and mechanics The GTA 6 1010 Murals activity initially requires you to read a specific Snapmatic post from an artist named 1010. It tells of a collaboration/cross-promotion with the manufacturer Grotti. Here’s the kicker: As far as we can tell, Snapmatic posts tend to disappear/get replaced as you advance through the campaign. Upon checking, it looks like 1010’s Snapmatic post remains active from the early to mid-point of chapter 3. This is roughly up to 55% story completion, so it’s just before you start the Cartel Heist arc. Assuming you’ve read 1010’s post, here’s what you need to do next: Go to specific locations that have 1010’s signature mark: a black and white orb that slightly resembles a meteor or an eyeball. Stand on or next to those marks. Your controller should vibrate telling you that you’re on the correct spot. Look for a fragmented mural in the vicinity. Open the Camera app on your phone and take a picture of the formed mural (R2 or RT). Map: 1010 Murals in Vice City The map below shows the locations of the five murals that you must take photos of. We’ve also included an icon for the reward that you obtain much later. Mural #1: Compliance Theater Travel to Mariner’s Highway in Downtown and look for Piker Financial Services. Off to the side, there’s a door that you can unlock stealthily if you already have the Snap Gun. If not, you could kick it down, though that would trigger an alarm. Likewise, there’s a worker in the next corridor, and they’ll warn you when you enter the building. Try to defuse the situation or incapacitate them without being seen by other NPCs. From there, ride the elevator to the rooftop, then climb up the ladder all the way to the top of the tower. 1010’s symbol is on a board, so just stand near it and take a photo of the mural below. Mural #2: Extraction Service This 1010 Mural in GTA 6 is directly north of the one that we mentioned earlier. Go to Catalan Boulevard and look for the New Quay Plaza. Head to the opposite side of the rooftop and look for the adjacent buildings with a mural. Mural #3: Loophole Architecture The next artwork is in Rockridge, specifically in a tenement building on Northbrook Drive. If it’s your first time entering this apartment complex, you’ll also find out that it’s a gang hideout and robbery opportunity. In any case, head up the elevator when you can and take a photo of the stadium across the street. Mural #4: You Signed the Terms and Conditions Okay, we’re going out on a limb by saying that this particular 1010 Mural in GTA 6 might cause headaches. It’s located on NE 2nd Avenue, which is just southwest of your apartment in Vice City. Here’s the problem: Once you arrive at the location, you’ll see 1010’s marker at street level. You’ll also notice the colorful tram station up ahead. The idea is to wait for the tram with unique design/colors, and then take a picture of it once it briefly stops at that station. The issue is that the specific train might take a while, which can be a hassle if you have to wait for too long. Note: If possible, try to check if your controller would vibrate when a generic train passes. Perhaps a photo of that could still be added to your tally. Mural #5: Privatized Pains Socialized Gains This one is on Barlow Street and it’s near Effluvia, the high-end bar and restaurant where you meet Brian and Lori as part of a main mission. Stand near the mark and take a photo of the stadium just across from your position. 1010 Murals reward location After taking a photo of all five murals, you’ll receive a message from 1010 congratulating you for your efforts. 1010 also sends a photo of the next location, but barely any other info. In any case, make your way to the southwestern part of Tequesta. There, you’ll see a garage with a keypad. The passcode is--you guessed it--the moniker of the person you’ve been talking to the whole time. Enter 1-0-1-0 to open the shutter door. Inside, complete with its own cutscene, is the ‘95 Grotti Cheetah. Oh, and this particular garage becomes yours, too, giving you one more slot for a registered car. That does it for our guide on where to find all 1010 Murals in Grand Theft Auto 6. If you’re still searching for other activities that reward awesome cars, we suggest tackling the NoFlushers mission , which leads to the mind-blowing speed demon known as the Truffade Thrax--i.e. Bugatti Chiron lookalike. title: How To Steal And Register Cars With Advanced Trackers In GTA 6
summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a massive world, and you can be sure that there are thousands of vehicles driving across the countryside at any given point in time. While the vast majority can be hijacked without worries--well, aside from cops that might see you--a select few have anti-theft devices that make them an unbearable hassle. Thankfully, there are ways to steal vehicles with Advanced Trackers. Advanced Trackers: How exactly do they work? The Advanced Trackers in GTA 6 can be seen if you scan most high-end vehicles like sports cars and luxury cars. Basically, if it looks expensive and sells for a high price, you can bet that it has an Advanced Tracker. Here’s how the device works: Stolen vehicles with a Standard Tracker ping their location only if (a) they’ve significantly slowed down or stopped, and (b) a police car is nearby. Advanced Trackers, meanwhile, ping their location if you go below a certain speed. You essentially need to put your pedal to the metal when driving them. Otherwise, the police would know your exact location. Given the risk, most fence NPCs in the game won’t even accept stolen vehicles with Advanced Trackers. Well, except for one fella: Randy. The legit method: Do missions for Randy Randy is the one NPC in the game that accepts stolen cars with Advanced Trackers, but there are some caveats: You meet Randy while tackling main missions in chapter 3. He’ll give you a task to steal a Zorrusso, which also nets you the Key Cloner, a tool that allows you to hijack keyless cars. At this point, Randy and various Pay ‘n’ Spray shops will start accepting stolen vehicles with Standard Trackers. He’ll also tell you that he has a “wishlist” of sorts: A dozen or so high-end cars that you need to boost and bring to his garage. Note that some targets do have Advanced Trackers. He’ll only accept these as long as they’re part of his wishlist. Since he’ll keep them, you won’t be able to own/register them at all. Again, you need to drive fast to prevent the tracker from triggering. But you also have to be careful since the sell value of the car will decrease depending on the damage. Now, let’s say you’ve completed all of Randy’s requests. Come chapter 4, Randy will give you one more mission. This time, you need to boost a Mamba GT. After that ordeal, you’ll be able to remove Advanced Trackers via Pay ‘n’ Spray shops in Leonida. Yes, you’ll finally be able to register/own all those high-end vehicles you keep seeing in Vice City. The exploit method: Have your partner drive it There’s also another method if you wish to steal cars with Advanced Trackers in GTA 6. It’s an exploit that involves fiddling around with partner controls. Here’s how to do it: Have your partner tag along while you’re exploring. Locate a car with an Advanced Tracker. Don’t do anything with it yet. Look for a car near it, one that only has a Standard Tracker or no tracker at all. Make sure you unlock that vehicle. Next, unlock the door of the car with the Advanced Tracker… and immediately exit it. Open the partner interface by holding L2/LT. Then, select “You Drive.” This will cause your partner to enter the last vehicle that you interacted with--i.e. the one with the Advanced Tracker. As for your own character, simply hop on to the other car that you jacked. Then, open the partner interface again and select “Follow.” (If your partner is driving the vehicle, they won’t trigger the tracker’s system.) Drive your lowly vehicle to Randy’s shop, and watch as your partner follows behind you at a leisurely pace. When you’re in front of Randy’s garage, simply switch to your partner and deliver the vehicle. That’s it. No police chases, no need to drive over the speed limit, and no panicking due to the tracker’s alarm potentially going off. title: GTA 6 Has Massive Underground Caves Worth Diving Into
summary: Take a break from all the car chases and crimes in Grand Theft Auto 6 , and relax in the quaint Emerald Springs resort. Oh, what's that? Is there something interesting nearby? Yes, it looks like a tourist attraction, the Selkie Hole, is worth a look. Perhaps there are hidden rewards that await you in the depths of the underwater cave. In This Article Where to find the Selkie Hole in Grand Theft Auto 6 The blue pools Cave diving for rewards and following the ropes More tunnels and meteorites Potential for more secrets: The Hollow Earth theory Where to find the Selkie Hole in Grand Theft Auto 6 The Selkie Hole in GTA 6 can be found in Kelly County. Specifically, it’s in a large nature reserve known as Emerald Springs. To get there, follow the road leading southeast out of Port Gellhorn or west from Hamlet. The blue pools Upon arriving, be sure to check the nearby scannables using your WAiNK app. Then, make your way to the western part of the park as shown on the map above. You’ll find a visually striking place, a pool with crystal clear blue water. From there, look for a small shed that has the Selkie Hole signage. This leads to the diving area, which also has Scuba Gear for you and your partner to equip. Likewise, note that the cave entrance here counts as a WAiNK Curiosity when scanned. Cave diving for rewards and following the ropes From the diving area, keep to the left as you go underwater. You’ll see a ropeline with arrows. The arrows actually point toward the exit which, in this case, is the diving area itself. So, for now, follow the rope as it leads in the opposite direction. Along the way, you’ll be able to pick up a couple of meteorites and the Explorer’s Knife legendary weapon. You’ll end up at the other end of the tunnel--i.e. the pool with clear blue water. Note: Pay attention to the remaining oxygen in your oxygen tank. You have to return to the diving area if you want to refill it or equip your Scuba Gear again. More tunnels and meteorites But that’s not the end of your deep dive since there are more underwater caves in GTA 6, and they’re in the same general area in the Emerald Springs. Return to the diving spot and, this time, keep to the right. You’ll see a warning not to go any further. Keep exploring the winding tunnel as it eventually leads you to the larger body of water in the nature reserve. We also took our time checking out other openings and tunnels, which dot the entire area. We even found additional meteorites for our tally. Moreover, if you do this in-game and open the world map, you’ll notice that certain cave systems have their own segmented outlines, which disappear if you zoom out. There are also sections on the map with a light blue hue and a shape akin to a spiral. These denote that you have to dive deeper, which leads to yet another layer of the underwater map. Note: This activity might not be for the faint of heart. Emerald Springs' cave systems have narrow tunnels that are almost pitch black. There are also segments where the ropes have been detached or buried, making navigation challenging. The atmosphere can make you feel a bit claustrophobic, so try to relax and get your bearings before delving deeper. Potential for more secrets: The Hollow Earth theory Perhaps there are more secrets to be found in the depths of Selkie Hole in GTA 6. One particular hint can even be seen along the road that leads to the diving area. It’s a poster that references the Hollow Earth Theory--i.e. there is a massive subterranean space under the crust where hidden entities dwell. Maybe they’re mole people, mutants, or dinosaurs. Who knows? Then again, this could all just be a red herring that leads nowhere. You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. title: How To Get A Helicopter In GTA 6
summary: You’ll spend so many hours driving across the state of Leonida in Grand Theft Auto 6 , that your feet will start to ache in the real world. But there are still other modes of travel that you can try out. And, yes, you can take to the skies as well on board a helicopter. In This Article Helicopter spawns in Grand Theft Auto 6 Early-game option: Buckingham Maverick Military helicopters in GTA 6 Amphibious helicopters Rooftop helipads in Vice City Helicopter spawns in Grand Theft Auto 6 As of the time of this writing, there’s no clear way to permanently own a helicopter in GTA 6. These vehicles can neither be saved near your safehouse, nor can they be delivered to wherever you are. That said, there are several areas where helicopters frequently spawn. For the most part, you should look at helipad markings on the map--i.e. “H” symbol on rooftops and facilities. We’ve got a few examples below. Early-game option: Buckingham Maverick The Buckingham Maverick is a great early-game pick if you just want to explore and reveal more of the map. To find it, simply travel along the main highway from Jason’s home and keep going southwest until you reach Southwind. To the right, you’ll see MHH Marque Hoppers, which has a Maverick conveniently parked on the pier. Military helicopters in GTA 6 While you’re in the area, you might be interested in getting a military helicopter in GTA 6. There are several options like the machine-gunning Buzzard, sleek Valkyrie, and beefy Cargobob. All of these are in the Mile Zero Base just a short distance away from Southwind. You must be careful, though, because this is a military base that’s on high alert. If you get spotted within its boundaries, you’ll be warned by police and soldiers. Dawdle for too long and you’ll be reported for committing a crime, earning an instant 4-star Wanted Level for good measure. Having countless troops, including those in armored vehicles, shooting at you is not a good way to start the day. Amphibious helicopters It’s also a good idea to find amphibious helicopters like the Nagasaki Sea Sparrow. One is near the speedway in the southwestern part of Hamlet, and the other is further west at the halfway point between the town and Watson Bay. (It’s also where you obtain the Dominator Buggy if you own the Ultimate Edition.) As the term implies, these types of choppers can take off/land on water, making them integral for thorough exploration of the seas surrounding Leonida. Rooftop helipads in Vice City There are many helicopters flying all over Vice City, and you can grab one of them by searching for the helipad icons on your map. Buildings with helipads on the roof tend to have interiors that you can enter, as well as elevators that can take you to the top floor. From there, you just need to hijack the vehicle and zip away to safety. These are just some of the GTA 6 helicopters that you can acquire. Keep returning to these locations if you want them to respawn. As for other vehicles that you can steal, don’t forget to check our articles about tanks , planes , and boats . You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. If you need more help navigating the massive game world and tackling its activities, be sure to check our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub .

title: I Was Wrong About GTA 6
summary: Some months ago, I wrote about how, even prior to its full reveal, we already knew what GTA 6 was going to be . Although not unique to the franchise by any means, GTA games had always followed a very clear formula, rarely upending it in any meaningful way. I strongly suspected that the 13-year wait for GTA 6 would result in a very pretty version of a very familiar game. As release approached, I worried that for all of the praise heaped upon its story and incredible level of detail, all of that was merely a veneer on the same game we've been playing for 25 years. And in many ways, that is true; at its most basic level, GTA 6 is still a game about driving from point A to point B, and maybe shooting some ne'er-do-wells when you get there. But I dramatically underestimated the impact of that veneer, and just how differently a familiar formula can feel when accompanied by impactful systems and relationships. The freeform nature of GTA 6's world, and the objectives you have over the course of a given mission, are largely identical to previous games. You can just drive around and make your own fun, or deal with violent drug smugglers, or pilot a boat or plane or car through a series of checkpoints. It's all very familiar on paper. But never before in a GTA game have I considered whether I have time to go and do one of those things because I have someone I care about waiting at home. Only rarely in a GTA have I decided to drive carefully, lest I face the consequences of doing almost anything I'd traditionally associate with a GTA game. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c38Opkxzqvc So much of GTA 6's focus is on the relationship between Lucia and Jason. I quickly found myself caring about them both, and for all of Rockstar's talk of their romantic relationship being optional, I truly can't fathom playing this in a way that doesn't fully embrace their love. And the way that permeates things even in Chapter 1--the phone calls, the text messages, the interactions at home--has forced some degree of role-playing on me. I check the time on my in-game phone not because I'm wondering if it's late enough to meet a contact in the woods, but because I want to be sure I'm home in time to hang out, whether that's talking, watching TV, or browsing our respective phones together. Despite the insistence of your boss, Brian, that you get down to a meeting spot for your next mission, I delayed doing so because it was a long drive late in the day, and the thought of leaving my partner hanging was unacceptable. Were that the only thing I was doing differently in GTA 6 than in past games, I think it would still fall into the category of veneer--a bit of narrative-laced framing that surrounds the usual chaos of going out and driving down sidewalks and blowing up cars. Instead, that more thoughtful approach to things extends to almost all of the moment-to-moment gameplay. I regularly drive the speed limit (something made much easier by the fantastic usage of the PS5's DualSense triggers ). I tend to stay on the road and in my lane, and well away from any pedestrians or other cars. I do frequently blow through red lights, but only after looking both ways. When I pull off a robbery, I tend to target other criminals, rather than stores. I routinely pull over when I need to use my phone while driving. I don't hijack random cars driving by--some 25 hours in, I've not done this most basic of actions in a GTA game even once. A small amount of this does stem from that urge to role-play as these characters. Jason and Lucia might be criminals, but they also feel like real people, and it's hard to imagine them running over innocent bystanders or smashing up their cars because you're intent on reaching your destination in as little time as possible. Additionally, the fact that you have ownership of your vehicle--which can suffer damage and require repairs, needs gas, and stores weapons and drugs you've stolen--makes it feel far less like the disposable vehicles of the past (including the character-specific vehicles of GTA 5). By placing more emphasis overall on money and making you carefully consider how it gets spent, I'm less willing to suffer a dent to my ride or risk attracting police attention. Driving carefully in GTA 6 is more worthwhile than ever The importance of your car also comes in part from both the increased difficulty of stealing any random vehicle you come across, the added value of your car (where you can reliably store things in the trunk), and the challenges of dealing with the police when you get a Wanted level. There's a sense of danger here that I've never felt before in a GTA game. Again, the role-playing factors here, as I don't want to "die" (such as you can), nor do I want to lose money, letting down my partner. I want to see them achieve their goals, but I also want to make the time I spend earning money mean something. Furthermore, the realistic nature of the world, both in terms of the visual fidelity and the many fine details contained within, make it harder to treat NPCs as chaff. In GTA 6, I'd feel bad if I ran over a person--or, heaven forbid, a dog or cat--rather than feeling they are collateral damage I forget about 10 seconds later. Even hostiles, like the random criminals who attempt to hijack your car, I deal with as delicately as possible, which is to say, I shoot them in the leg; my body count in this game would regularly be eclipsed by five minutes of random gameplay in a past GTA game. Although I wouldn't have realized it before playing, this is what I wanted a GTA game to be at this point in my life. I'm less interested in the random chaos that made me fall in love with GTA 2 and 3 back in the day; instead, I want strong characterization, a story that I feel invested in, and gameplay systems that both reward and encourage thoughtful play. I no longer want to be an undeniable force that everything in Leonida revolves around; I want to exist as another believable aspect of this world. This is not to say I won't ever go wild when I get my hands on a tank and wreak some havoc. But unlike in the past, doing so will be only a temporary distraction, not the main attraction. For that to be the case, and for me to be happy about it, is GTA 6's most remarkable accomplishment.

title: Xbox Game Pass Kicks Off December With Horror, Cozy Adventures, And More
summary: One last month of 2026 brings two more waves of Xbox Game Pass titles to close out the year. Subscribers can once again look forward to some new arrivals in the Xbox Game Pass library, ranging from gruesome co-op action to wholesome adventures featuring helpful mice on a mission. These announcements typically come in two waves, with a sneak peek split between them, so while this list isn’t complete yet, we do know what you can expect in the first half of December. As usual, we’ll update this page once Xbox reveals the full lineup for this first batch. For now, you can look forward to an eclectic mix of games, starting with The Outlast Trials . Released in 2024, it’s a co-op survival-horror game that throws a team of up to four players into a gauntlet of deadly trials, where evasion is key to victory. You can also play it solo, and if the onslaught of festive season cheerfulness is getting to you, then this will be a nice–but brutal–change of pace. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hCgiwsIUI4g If you’d prefer to focus on the coziness of the season, then Hela: Of Mice and Magic looks like a fun time. Set in a magical forest inspired by Scandinavian lands, the game follows a group of mice on a journey to help people, at the behest of an old witch who can’t make the trip herself. This is also a day-one release for Xbox Game Pass, and it’ll be joined by World of Tanks Blitz on the same day. On December 3, Freestyle Football 2 launches, bringing fast-paced, 5v5 multiplayer street soccer to Xbox and PC, and on December 14, you can grab Nubby’s Number Factory, a roguelite game all about making big numbers. Xbox Game Pass December Wave 1 Games December 1 The Outlast Trials (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) — Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass Hela: Of Mice and Magic (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) — Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass World of Tanks Blitz December 3 Freestyle Football 2 December 14 Nubby’s Number Factory If you missed it, November brought a solid selection of releases. The first wave added the dungeon-crawling roguelike deck-building game Dungeon Crawlers to more Game Pass tiers, along with Warhammer Survivors and John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando. The Game Pass library expanded further later in November, with some Paw Patrol fun for the kiddos, High on Life 2, and the pretty good long-distance stealth game Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2.

title: I Was Wrong About GTA 6
summary: I expected GTA 6 to be a pretty version of a familiar game. It is, but there's much more to it than that.
